title: A Portrait for the Winter
premise: Astrid Dravenmoor returns to Hollowmere House to appraise it for probate, only to find the house cataloguing her back — doors that count themselves, rooms that remember her childhood, and an imaginary friend named Wren waiting on the porch, unchanged after thirty years. The founders of the house built a bargain with something beneath the well: a ritual of belonging, renewed each winter, that keeps the town fed and the dead quiet. Astrid must finish the interrupted ritual before the well refills at solstice — but completing it means choosing who is bound inside and who walks free. She ends it by taking the founders' place herself for one night, letting Wren go free, and sealing the well with her own name written in the ledger instead of a sacrifice.
about_author: Casper Amberdale is the pen name of a former land surveyor who spent a decade mapping properties in remote northern counties, where every deed hides a story. They write horror about places that refuse to be measured.

chapters.title: The Deed and the Dark
chapters.summary: Astrid arrives at Hollowmere House on a gray November afternoon to appraise it for probate. POV: Astrid. The house feels wrong in small ways — cold spots, a porch light already burning. Emotional beat: professional detachment beginning to crack as she recognizes details she shouldn't know.

chapters.title: Doors That Count Themselves
chapters.summary: Surveying the interior, Astrid counts eleven doors; recounting gives thirteen, then nine. POV: Astrid. She finds her own childhood drawings tucked in a wall cavity. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into certainty that the house knows her.

chapters.title: Wren on the Porch
chapters.summary: At dusk, Astrid finds Wren — her imaginary friend from age six — sitting on the porch steps, unchanged, asking why she took so long. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: vertiginous joy curdling into terror as memory floods back.

chapters.title: What the Well Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren explains the house's bargain: the founders' ritual kept something below the well asleep, renewed each winter solstice. The last one was interrupted in 1994 — the year Astrid's family fled. POV: alternating Astrid and Wren. Emotional beat: reluctant understanding.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Names
chapters.summary: In the cellar, Astrid finds the founders' ledger: generations of names, each crossed out at solstice, each a person 'given to belong.' Her grandmother's name is last, uncrossed. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: grief and betrayal — her family didn't flee; they defaulted.

chapters.title: The Town That Looks Away
chapters.summary: Astrid drives into Hollowmere village for supplies; the locals are warm but evasive, warning her off the house with practiced smiles. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: isolation deepening — the whole town is complicit in the arrangement.

chapters.title: Rooms That Remember
chapters.summary: Overnight, the house rearranges itself around Astrid's memories: her childhood bedroom reappears, her mother's voice hums through the walls. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: seduction — the house offers belonging at a price.

chapters.title: The First Refill
chapters.summary: The well water rises overnight, black and patient. Frost patterns form handprints on the windows from the outside. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: urgency — whatever waits below is waking early because the debt is overdue.

chapters.title: Descendants of the Founders
chapters.summary: Astrid tracks down Edith Marlowe, great-granddaughter of the lead founder, who confirms the ritual and admits the town has been feeding it substitutes for decades. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: moral revulsion — justice was never part of the bargain.

chapters.title: Edith's Confession
chapters.summary: Edith reveals the 1994 interruption: Astrid's grandmother refused to give a name and tried to end it, dying in the attempt. Astrid was meant to be the next entry. POV: Edith (flashback interwoven). Emotional beat: fury and resolve — Astrid decides to finish what her grandmother started.

chapters.title: The Ritual's Architecture
chapters.summary: Studying the founders' papers, Astrid learns the ritual requires three acts: naming, offering, and sealing — performed by someone the house accepts as its own. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: grim focus; she begins preparing, counting doors until they hold steady at twelve.

chapters.title: Wren's Price
chapters.summary: Wren confesses their nature: not imaginary, but the previous offering, given the house as a companion so it wouldn't be lonely between winters. Freeing Wren means replacing them. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: heartbreak — Astrid refuses to accept the terms.

chapters.title: The House Appraises Back
chapters.summary: The house turns hostile: doors vanish, hallways loop, the appraisal report writes itself with Astrid's name in the ledger. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: claustrophobic panic as she realizes the house has been evaluating her all along.

chapters.title: Neighbors Below
chapters.summary: Through the well, Astrid hears the accumulated dead — including her grandmother — whispering fragments of the sealing rite the founders never wrote down. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: eerie communion; the dead want the cycle broken too.

chapters.title: Solstice Eve
chapters.summary: Snow seals the roads. Edith arrives to help, bringing the founder's iron key. The well is nearly full. POV: alternating Astrid and Edith. Emotional beat: tense camaraderie on the edge of the deadline.

chapters.title: Naming
chapters.summary: First act of the ritual: Astrid speaks her name into the ledger, claiming the house as hers. The walls settle; the doors hold at twelve. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: terrifying empowerment — ownership cuts both ways.

chapters.title: Offering
chapters.summary: Second act: the house demands an offering. Astrid offers her memories of Hollowmere instead of a life — and the house, hungry for belonging rather than blood, hesitates. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: desperate improvisation against ancient rules.

chapters.title: The Well Refills
chapters.summary: The negotiation fails; the well crests and the thing beneath rises into the cellar. Edith holds the door while Astrid descends. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: raw survival terror amid rising water and older hungers.

chapters.title: Sealing
chapters.summary: Third act: Astrid writes her own name across the ledger's final page and speaks the dead's whispered rite, binding herself to the house for one night each winter in place of any sacrifice. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: sacrificial clarity — justice made by choice, not law.

chapters.title: Letting Wren Go
chapters.summary: With the seal set, Wren's bond dissolves. They say goodbye on the porch at dawn; Wren fades smiling, finally finished. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: bittersweet release — love means opening the door outward.

chapters.title: Appraisal Complete
chapters.summary: Astrid files her report, valuing the house honestly, and buys it herself with her savings. The town watches, uncertain whether to thank or fear her. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: quiet defiance — she stays because belonging should be chosen.

chapters.title: One Night Each Winter
chapters.summary: Epilogue: each solstice, Astrid lights the porch lamp and keeps the doors counted; the well stays still, and sometimes her grandmother's humming joins hers through the walls. POV: Astrid. Emotional beat: hard-won peace — the price paid, the home earned.
